_comment: Board registry. Boards are identified by the MCU NAME in the data dictionary (mcu_candidates), never by port: the mainboard is the board that answers as stm32f401xc, the toolhead the one that answers as stm32f103xe. serial_hint is only a prior (stock printer.cfg: [mcu U_1] = /dev/ttyS0 = mainboard, [mcu] = /dev/ttyS2 = toolhead). expect_config holds the constants the live printer's klippy.log reports for each board; a firmware image whose data dictionary disagrees is refused. 'parameters' records what is settled about the flash layout; a board whose parameters.status is 'unresolved' is NEVER written (see runner._check_parameters). Derivation of every value: mcu/params.json and mcu/README.md.

toolhead.label: Toolhead board (extruder, hotend, probe)

parameters.clock_ref: 8 MHz external crystal (STM32_CLOCK_REF_8M); HSE is certain, 8 MHz is likely
open_questions: Does this printer's toolhead run Katapult or the stock factory bootloader? A firmware built for the wrong application offset does not boot, and only an ST-Link can recover a board whose bootloader is missing or unknown.
If it runs Katapult: its application offset (0x08002000 for the community 8 KiB build) must be read from the live bootloader, and its baud rate (250000 or 500000) is compile-time.
If it runs the stock bootloader: nothing documents a serial flash protocol for it, and the stock application offset is unknown (0x08008000 is only inferred from the Q2 toolhead).

toolhead.recovery: Re-flash the saved application image through Katapult (eitri-mcuflash rollback toolhead). If Katapult itself is gone the board is only recoverable with a soldered SWD header and an ST-Link V2.

mainboard.label: Mainboard (X/Y/Z steppers, bed, chamber)

open_questions: A direct read of the stock board's SCB->VTOR is still missing; 0x08008000 is derived from community images that boot on this board (mcu/README.md).
The HSE crystal frequency (8 MHz) is inferred; a mismatch would bring the board up at the wrong baud rate and it would not connect (recoverable through the SD bootloader).

mainboard.recovery: Copy the stock qd_mcu.bin to the root of a FAT32 microSD card, insert it in the mainboard slot (case must be opened) and press the mainboard RESET button; the board's stock SD bootloader (at 0x08000000, which Eitri never writes) flashes it on its own.
